rules.name: Communication Breakdown
rules.description: In the first turn of the game, if the first Order Die drawn from the cup is one of yours, the enemy can decide that the dice is put back into the cup and a new Order Die is drawn instead.

rules.name: Forward Artillery Doctrine
rules.description: French Armies get one free Inexperienced or Regular artillery unit. This unit can be any anti-tank gun of field artillery piece in the French Army list (except Heavy Artillery). This unit is in addition to the number of artillery units normally available.

rules.name: Hurriedly Conscripted Reserves
rules.description: If the force includes 3 or more Inexperienced Infantry Sections, then it may include a free  inexperienced infantry section identical to the cheapest one already purchased. This free section is in addition to the units chosen from whatever selector is used.

rules.name: Sacred Ground
rules.description: The Frenchmen are fighting for their own homeland against the very invaders which pushed them out in 1940. The stakes are high and the grim determination of the French fighting man is at its zenith. Any Regular or Veteran Infantry unit may be stubborn for +1pt per model.

rules.name: La Resistance
rules.description: By October 1944, nearly 400,000 Frenchmen and women had flocked to the banner of Free France to stand against the Axis invaders in one of the various resistance movements. Thousands of resistors were drafted into the Free French Army as it advanced. A Late-war Free French force may include a 10-man FFI squad for free if it includes two or more FFI squads of any size. The free FFI squad must pay the points for any upgrades it is equipped with.

rules.name: Local Area Knowledge
rules.description: As thousands of French soldiers advanced across their homeland, each town, village or farmstead would be a return home for some. If a unit’s own knowledge of each area was not enough, resistance groups would often be on hand to act as guides, delighted to see the French Army back on home soil. A Late-war Free French force does not suffer the –1 penalty for attempting to bring vehicles onto the table.

rules.name: Fighting French
rules.description: Allied planners expected the 1st Free French Brigade to hold the Bir Hakeim position for 10 days. They held out for 15 days, and twice refused formal requests for their surrender before fighting their way out of the encirclement. Winston Churchill declared that from this point on, they should be known as the ‘Fighting French’. All units re-roll unsuccessful morale checks, the second result stands.

rules.name: Colonial Veterans
rules.description: All members of the 1st Free French Brigade were professional soldiers from the French colonial forces, or Foreign Legionnaires, veterans of the Spanish Civil War and the 1940 expedition to Norway. No Inexperienced troops of any kind may be used.

rules.name: Sous-Officer
rules.description: Once per game, as soon as an officer has been removed as a casualty, the NCO of the nearest infantry squad within 12” of the officer when he became a casualty takes over command of the reinforced platoon. He gains the benefits of a Second Lieutenant, thus granting +1 to all order and morale tests to his own unit and those within 6” of himself. The newly promoted NCO remains with his original squad and the officer is still removed as a casualty as per normal. The newly promoted officer is also granted the “You men snap to action!” ability.

rules.name: Baptism of Fire
rules.description: Units must be purchased as either Regular or Inexperienced.

rules.name: Gyro-stabilisers
rules.description: Veteran Crews do not suffer the -1 to hit when issued an Advance order, this do not apply to co-axial Machineguns.

rules.name: Modern Comunication
rules.description: Free French units do not apply the -1 to the order test to move onto the table; use basic morale instead.

rules.name: Fire And Manoeuvre
rules.description: Models armed with BARs do not suffer the -1 penalty to Advance and Fire.

rules.name: Relentless Pursuit
rules.description: Infatry squad of the French Expeditionary Corp may make a Run move after both sides have set up, but before the first turn of the game. During this move, they cannot assault enemy units and cannot be targeted by enemies in Amnush.

sharedRules.name: 'Qui ose gagne!'
sharedRules.description: To represent their special training and motivation, units of Free French SAS have the fanatics special rule.

sharedRules.name: Tenir vos armes!
sharedRules.description: The brave crews of these guns kept firing even at Stukas making direct strafing runs on them. These units may never voluntarily use the Down order.

sharedRules.name: The Legion
sharedRules.description: French Foreign Legionnaires can re-roll morale checks to stay on the table.

sharedRules.name: Espirit de Corps
sharedRules.description: Units with Espirits de Corps special rule remove D2 pins whenever they pass an order test, instead of the usual one pin.

rules.description: Once per game, at the beginning of any turn before the first die is drawn from the dice bag. Roll a D6 and apply modifiers: Inexperienced -1, Veteran +1. On a 4+, the player activating the Intelligence Officer may choose a die from the bag for the first activation. If both players attempt to activate this ability simultaneously, each must roll 1D6. The higher score wins and immediately uses this ability, but the losing player may attempt to use his ability on another turn instead.

rules.name: Inspiring Presence
rules.description: Upon receiving his order dice (except for Down), a chaplain may select one friendly unit within 6" and roll a D6, applying the following modifiers: Inexperienced -1, Veteran +1. On a 4+, the chaplain may remove 1 pin from the selected unit.

rules.name: Non Combatant
rules.description: The chaplain is there to support the soldiers, not win battles. A chaplain unit cannot be used to claim or contest objectives.

rules.name: Self-defence only
rules.description: Clergymen are not soldiers and will not take part in hostile actions - they cannot fire any weapon, nor assault enemy units. If your chaplain is equipped with a pistol, it can only be used in close quarters if the enemy assaults him (including firing it at the assaulting enemies as a reaction, if applicable).

rules.name: Gun assembly
rules.description: To simulate the fact that the gun was actually transported disassembled, when the gun is unlimbered the artillery unit suffers a pin. When the gun is limbered, the mule team (and consequently the transported artillery unit) suffers a pin.

rules.name: Stubborn (Mule)
rules.description: When taking an order test and doubles are rolled, the mules become stubborn and refuse to cooperate even if the order test was passed. Place the order dice to Down and add 1 pin marker to th eteam. This rule does not apply if Fubar is rolled.

rules.name: Fighting Elite
rules.description: The chasseurs of the Chasseurs Alpins are highly trained and highly motivated fighting men with a fearsome reputation. All infantry and headquarters units in the reinforced platoon must be Veteran.

rules.name: Mountain Mobile
rules.description: All infantry and headquarters units in the reinforced platoon are equipped with skis and ignore movement penalties for snow and other winter conditions.

rules.name: Always prepared
rules.description: If the reinforced platoon is used in any scenario which includes the Frostbite rule for French forces, cold weather clothing must be taken for every headquarters and infantry unit.
